- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline at 2–4% below peak unless sentiment turns bullish.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting sharp drop after recent high), check sentiment for reversal signals — if sentiment remains neutral or bullish, delay correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in early periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is uncertain or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “low-high-low” cycles, model tends to lag in recognizing turning points; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true turning point if sentiment confirms reversal.
